reviews.text: Most amazing place, love that they’re no kill ♥️
They took the baby duck we found and its going to be okay. So grateful this place exists and that people donate to help wildlife.
Came to drop off an abandoned baby squirrel, got to pet a horse. Seems like a good day to me
They quickly took in the baby squirrel I found, and even told me about his health and that he would probably be okay! Very sweet staff, you can tell they genuinely care about the animals here.

Had to take unfortunately bring in some baby squirrels that were displaced and left in our garden.  They took them with extreme care and we were able to donate and support their cause.  If you ever come across an animal that you can safely engage or use animal control, make sure they bring here.

I took an abandoned baby dove to their place and loved the way they received us and the bird. They took it in, gave it a shower, fed it and took a really good care of the bird. Just love the way they do the service

Great parking very clean.  Inside very clean and organized staff very friendly.

We took in a bird that my daughter found on the sidewalk.  Seemed injured the it couldn't move or fly.  We originally thought it broke it's legs because they were very flimsy and pulled backwards.  He was laying on extremely HOT 🔥  concrete and slowly moving towards the middle of the highway in a high traffic area.

Thankfully after the technician X-rayed him/her she said the legs seemed fine and that usually they hit objects at high velocities which leaves them dumb foinded or discombobulated and paralyzed for about 3 days but eventually they regain strength and and their bodies re-awaken eventually  rehabilitating themselves and be able to fly.
We are so lucky to have this very special organization. They are doing Gods work for these little creatures.
The BEST wildlife hospital!! Thanks for helping Texan wildlife!
It's a great place
I brought in an injured squirrel. The lady I spoke with on the phone, the lady that took him to the back and the other lady that inputted my information were all really nice!!
I have dropped off two wild animals here and they have a very nice facility to get them rehabilitated.
Dropped off an orphaned raccoon that we rescued and the process was very fast took us about 10 minutes start to finish. He is in great hands!

Very disappointing intake experience.

The staff member was indifferent, showed zero care for the duckling's background, and abruptly rushed it away without letting us say goodbye.
Wildlife rehab requires empathy and heart, not just a mechanical routine.
Dropped off baby pigeon we found and it was an easy drop off process.

My daughter recently began volunteering at the Houston SPCA, and while she was volunteering, I spent some time exploring the facility with my sons. We had such a wonderful experience.

From the moment we arrived, everyone we encountered was welcoming, kind, and helpful. The staff and volunteers were friendly and made us feel comfortable and appreciated as visitors.

The facility itself is beautiful, clean, and incredibly well maintained. The grounds are thoughtfully landscaped and provide a peaceful, inviting environment for both people and animals. You can tell a great deal of care goes into maintaining the property and ensuring the animals are comfortable.

My son especially loved visiting the cats and meeting some of the dogs. It was heartwarming to see how much attention and care the animals receive while they wait for their forever homes.

What stood out most was the positive atmosphere. The Houston SPCA is clearly a place filled with compassionate people who genuinely care about animals and the community they serve.

We're grateful for the opportunity for my daughter to volunteer here and look forward to spending more time at such a wonderful organization. Thank you to everyone who helps make this place so special.
This is a clean and very welcoming facility, for humans and others. ❤️🐦
Thank you for helping to save this little
Dropped off a baby bird
We brought an injured bird in and they took care of him

Awesome facility!! It was surprisingly hard to find someone willing to take some abandoned racoon pups, SPCA was the only one we could find. Super friendly staff and they reassured us what would happen with the animals and their current status.
Awesome service
They took in a wounded cardinal I found, once it is fully healthy they will release it to fly home. A donation helps them to aid our wildlife in the area, please be kind
Very clean and well kept.

I live in the country and we have dogs and cats and chickens. And they are always bringing me hurt animals and this is the place I trust to take care and rehabilitate and return to the wild where they belong. I really appreciate this place more than anything. Thank you guys for caring so much.
Amazingly great for helping to save a turtle who'd been caught by a fishing hook.

I could not give a five stars, I’m not sure if they really going to save the little squirrel I dropped off today, hopefully they don’t let her die or put it to sleep. I pray this place help her to live and release her to a safe place.

Wonderful resource to advocate and care for the animals of our community.

Amazing place
Incredible facility! Top notch staff!

They also have an adoption center, If you want to adopt cats, dogs, or even small mammals like guinea pigs and hamsters, this is the place. Give them orphaned animals a new life and support this amazing cause. Planning on coming back to donate or volunteer.

We were so pleasantly surprised. The facility is very clean and animals seemed well cared for. The only knock is that it took an HOUR to fill out the adoption paperwork and adopt. They definitely need to fix that bc everyone went from excited to adopted to very frustrated!
I found an injured bird and they immediately took her in and cared for her.

On 10Nov25, I called this organization about getting a broken wing Hawk.  I could not get straight answers from anyone.  One particular individual in the call center was especially unprofessional, combative, and uncooperative.  I did not like being given the run around, so I expressed my thoughts.  This equaled a threat to these people who then put a precinct 4 constable on me.  I made them "uncomfortable" is what Brooke, the director told me today, 11Nov25.  The terrible treatment I received is a direct reflection of the Director's leadership.  There is no accountability under her.  No city or county tax funds should be used as long as the current leadership is there.  Let it be know, this is not the first time I've come here.  I brought a little song bird in about 3 years ago.  Night and day with the treatment then and now.
I’ll gladly come back again.
The phone guy during the night that I tried to call to help because I saw abandoned orphaned kitten on the street, the phone guy was extremely rude and doesn’t care of other lives animals. Very rude.
The Wildlife center is a godsend to injured and orphaned.

I was deeply saddened because yesterday I saw a small turtle crossing the street. I picked it to avoid it getting run over. I proceeded to drop it off at the SPCA wildlife center around 9:30ish and I was told to go leave it in a “woodsy” area. I was even given a name of park I could go leave it at. I said absolutely not! First of all, I cannot imagine in this day and age going to drop off a turtle and then someone accuses me of abandoning it. So I declined and with a not very nice attitude the young lady took it from me at the Wild life center. I hope the turtle was checked out by a vet and finds a loving home or SPCA finds an appropriate park to release it at.
Quick to answer my phone call and to see the injured bird I found
They have taken in two wild animals from me - one baby heron and one baby squirrel. The facility is clean, seems well organized, the staff is professional and caring.
We dropped off a white herin with broken wings 🪽 Aspca was professional and cares about the Animals health care …
The staff here are always so nice and so helpful. Very caring.

Great for wildlife protection.
Great place
I brought in an injured baby bunny. Lady up front was so nice. The facility is awesome.  If I didn’t live so far away, I would volunteer to work there.

This place is amazing, the people working there are super fast and sweet, I  bring  a baby raccoon and a baby opossum, and they take both. The place is clean everything is clean and well  care, I definitely  recommend Houston SPCA.

As soon as we arrived, a staff member identified the bird and explained what was wrong within minutes. The facility was very neat and organized, and we felt great knowing he was in good hands. We highly recommend this place! It’s amazing that you can bring in an injured wild animal and they accept them with open arms. We were more than happy to make a donation.
Always professional.  So happy we have a place to get help for the vulnerable creatures.
Awesome facility and staff!
Very professional and friendly service.
A fabulous facility.  They were so kind and took care of the little baby birds I had found.
Dropped off many wildlife babies here, the process is easy and fast.
Took in a wounded Blue Jay fledgling. The process was super quick and the staff were really friendly.

I found a bird that I suspected of being hit by a car on the road and brought it into the wildlife center at the Houston SPCA. I didn't think to ask her name but the woman who greeted me from the front desk upon entering was so lovely! She was upbeat despite the seemingly overwhelming amount of animals they intake everyday. She was kind and helpful to at least seven different people I saw come in while being there for only around 10 minutes. She was quick and efficient in triaging each animal, whilst maintaining such a welcoming demeanor the whole time. Even when people described things that they had done to "care for" the animal they brought in that wouldn't necessarily in line with best practice, She gave no indication of annoyance and didn't belittle them or make them feel like they did the wrong thing, she only thanked them for bringing the animal in. If you find an injured animal, look up the Houston SPCA wildlife centers website and follow their instructions on how to determine whether or not to bring the animal in. After doing so, if you have determined that they can help treat the animal, I would absolutely recommend bringing it into them! Again, they do care for hundreds of animals weekly and only have limited resources so if you do think you have found an animal that needs care, make sure it follows their guidelines before bringing it in or call and they can advise you. Also consider making a donation, even a few dollars, while you're there!

Tell me why I called trying to help this bird which I witnessed his mom die and took him in, and this lady was criticizing me instead of helping. Telling me I shouldn’t do that and all types of crap. But I’m thankful that they will take care of him. Apparently they get no government funding so I’ll try my best to donate from time to time. So sad they don’t have enough staff to give us updates on the babies :(

Great and beautiful facility, won't bring animals here again. The in person interaction left me feeling like a should go somewhere else. Tried to tell me how the baby bird would be better with its mother but wouldn't listen to the fact I have 10 rescue barn cats, so my property is never a good place for a nest. Like didn't even want to listen to me, i had already saved thr bird from my carts & a snake when i tried giving it a makeshift nest. Call for an update and they don't have the staff to do that. I had asked in person if they had social media where they could post updates for people to follow and that was an abrupt, NO!  So I'll go to another place my friend recommended next time. Like I was disappointed every interaction here. Really sucks as an animal advocate and lover.

This place is really cute, the people are so nice and friendly, very understanding too they talked me through on what I did good and bad when bringing my baby birds I found. Really recommend going here amazing experience!

We watched a Coopers hawk hit a car. The bird survived and we took it here. I hear she made a full recovery and was released.
I can't thank these people enough for the work that they do.
Except to keep donating ...and we do and so should you.
